name: Bob Badal
current_role: Co-founder, Strive Health (listed as Chief Revenue Officer); advisory partner, a16z Bio + Health
profile: Healthcare executive who co-founded Strive Health (Denver value-based kidney-care provider, valued ~$2B) in 2018. Before that he spent 12+ years at DaVita running health-plan and provider network contracting and strategy (a $2.5B+ revenue portfolio) and served as President of DaVita Kidney Care's Latin America operations. Now also an a16z Bio + Health advisory partner and board member at several health companies.
interesting_fact: At DaVita he was President of Latin America Operations for DaVita Kidney Care, after a decade-plus in health-plan network development and hospital administration.
deep_cut_fact: Studied economics and law at Trinity University in San Antonio before his USC Marshall MBA; in 2017, a year before Strive, he co-founded WaveHealth, an electronic patient-reported-outcomes (ePRO) company.

public_contacts.value: nleatherman@strivehealth.com (Strive Health Director of Communications & PR, published media contact)

notes: Low public profile. Strive's team page currently shows Riopelle and Stokes; Badal's Strive title (CRO) comes from secondary sources, and his a16z role suggests he may be less operational at Strive now.

name: Jonathan Ng
current_role: Founder & CEO, Iterative Health (formerly Iterative Scopes), AI for gastroenterology
profile: Singapore-trained physician (MBBS, NUS) who founded Iterative Health in 2017 while studying at MIT/Harvard. The Cambridge, MA company applies computer vision and AI to GI endoscopy, IBD clinical-trial recruitment and research, and is valued at ~$1B. He is based in New York.
interesting_fact: He says that at an early business-school competition, judges were 'mistaking AI for artificial insemination'.
deep_cut_fact: His path to entrepreneurship began when he broke his wrist in a car accident in his third year of medical practice in Singapore; the pause made him look at the whole health system. He admits he 'had no idea what an MBA was' when he applied, and the Iterative idea came 3-4 months after arriving at MIT.
notes: Physician-founder; has done several podcasts (Physician-Executive Series, Third Spacing), so open to interviews. No published press email found.

name: Barney Hussey-Yeo
current_role: Founder & CEO, Cleo (AI financial assistant, London/US)
profile: Former data scientist who co-founded Cleo with Aleksandra Wozniak after meeting at Entrepreneur First in 2015. Cleo is a conversational AI money assistant for Gen Z, known for its humorous tone, now mostly US-focused, with ~$330M ARR reported in 2026 and a $1B+ valuation.
interesting_fact: He argues humour was central to Cleo's success: 'Humor wasn't branding. It was a behavioural unlock.' Cleo's AI adjusts its tone based on user behaviour and stress signals.
deep_cut_fact: Cleo started as a scratch-his-own-itch project: he wanted a better way to track his own spending, met co-founder Aleksandra Wozniak at company builder Entrepreneur First, and raised a £2M seed led by LocalGlobe for the chatbot. He guards his mornings for deep work - no meetings, Slack or notifications.
notes: Active speaker (HumanX, UK tech podcasts) and listed on Qwoted as a media source. Cleo site blocks automated fetching, so press contact could not be verified; check its press page manually. Avoid leaning on his earlier employer (payday lender Wonga) in outreach. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane; later fields used direct fetches only.
